name: Maiden Acoustic
reference: The acoustic intros of Dance of Death (Dance of Death, 2003, Sarm West London) and Dream of Mirrors (Brave New World, 2000, Guillaume Tell Paris), both prod. Kevin Shirley with Steve Harris: bright, picked steel-string acoustic under the clean/harmony guitars, dry, with only the room around it. Also Journeyman (Dance of Death), Maiden's one fully acoustic song
rig: Which guitarist played the studio acoustics, and on which instrument, isn't documented for either record. Live, Janick Gers plays a Gibson Chet Atkins semi-acoustic (a steel-string acoustic-electric with a piezo pickup) for Dance of Death (Wikipedia, from Premier Guitar's 2010 rig gallery) and, per fan sites, Dream of Mirrors, so the parts are piezo-amplified steel-string acoustic in the band's own hands. Kevin Shirley's documented method on Dance of Death: the band live in the studio, Murray and Gers in a separate room with their amps, guitars through Neve 8069 pres, a Drawmer 1961 EQ and a UREI 1176; 'I didn't add any reverb, other than perhaps some on the orchestra on two songs', room mics instead, and the parts fitted together 'mainly with panning rather than EQ'. He suggested recording Brave New World the same live way. Emulated here as: electric -> Diamond optical compressor (the 1176 leveller) -> electric pre-voiced to a piezo, into a NAM capture of a piezo pickup re-recorded on a Rode condenser -> Taylor 816 steel-string acoustic IRs (M251 tube condenser), a different IR per side for a double-tracked pair -> a small wood room and a studio live room, both under 1.1 s
notes: REBUILT for the Dance of Death / Dream of Mirrors intros. The old chain (compressor -> Boss AC-3 -> Martin / J-45 body IRs, 480L Large Hall + Small Wood Room) measured darker than the dry DI itself: 2-5 kHz at -27.2 dB of the band energy, centroid 686 Hz, i.e. a boomy, muffled electric rather than a steel string, with ~3.5 s of reverb; offline renders show the AC-3 capture and these body IRs both take top end away (AC-3 alone: 2-5 kHz -34 dB). The new chain keeps 2 NAM blocks on the instance: slot 1 (boost, on) = Diamond Compressor, comp 5 (levels the picking the way Shirley's 1176 did; it also keeps the crest at ~15 dB so the bus limiter isn't hitting pick attacks); slot 2 (drive, on) = 'Acoustic piezo to microphone' NAM (a piezo pickup re-recorded on a Rode condenser) fed by the electric with a piezo pre-EQ (-6 dB 100 Hz shelf, -4 dB 250, +3 dB 1.6 kHz, +6 dB 3.5 kHz, +6 dB 8 kHz shelf) so the magnetic pickup's low-mid hump reads as a piezo; then L = Taylor 816 'M251 Pz1' IR, R = Taylor 816 'M251 SB1' IR, each with a body EQ (-8 dB 100 Hz shelf, -4 dB 250, -1 dB 650, +1 dB 1.6 kHz, +8 dB 3.5 kHz, +7 dB 8 kHz shelf) to cut the boom and open the strings. Measured offline: 2-5 kHz -8.9 dB, centroid ~1180 Hz, low<250 -5.9 dB. The guitars on the record and the Chet Atkins live are steel strings, so a Taylor steel-string IR is the nearest honest match; no Gibson Chet Atkins capture or IR exists in the catalog, and nothing makes an electric fully acoustic (best on the neck pickup, picked lightly). Stereo double: the two IRs panned hard left/right with Align wobble 0.15, like two acoustic takes panned apart (Shirley fitted parts by panning). Ambience, kept short for the crackles the owner hears on long tails (and dry like the records): echo block (always on; SW8/SW9 don't reach this instance) = reverb only, Lexicon 480L Small Wood Room, 1.0 s IR at 12%, standing in for the Sarm West room mics; slot 6 / R4 = Sunset Sound Studio 3 live room, mono, trimmed to 0.8 s (RT60 ~0.5 s) at 15%. Longest tail 1.0 s, both IRs together 1.8 s of convolution (was 2.0 s + 1.5 s, the Large Hall capped from 3.5 s). Levels: rendered offline with rigsim --exact to -15 LUFS (clean/acoustic target, D22); not yet measured on the live rig.
